claims.claim: The tower at Wardenclyffe was 187 feet tall.
claims.quote: By the end of 1902 the tower reached its full height of 187 feet.

claims.claim: Tesla abandoned the tower/project.
claims.quote: The people living around Wardenclyffe noticed the Tesla plant seemed to have been abandoned without notice.

claims.claim: The site is at Shoreham, Long Island.
claims.quote: Wardenclyffe is located near the Shoreham Post Office and Shoreham Fire House on Route 25A in Shoreham, Long Island, New York.

claims.claim: Tesla intended to transmit messages across the Atlantic Ocean.
claims.quote: Tesla intended to transmit messages, telephony, and even facsimile images across the Atlantic Ocean to England and to ships at sea based on his theories of using the Earth to conduct the signals.

claims.claim: Tesla planned to use the Earth itself as the conductor, sending messages, telephony and facsimile images to England and to ships at sea.
claims.quote: Tesla intended to transmit messages, telephony, and even facsimile images across the Atlantic Ocean to England and to ships at sea based on his theories of using the Earth to conduct the signals.

claims.claim: J. P. Morgan gave Tesla $150,000.
claims.quote: Morgan signed a contract with Tesla in March 1901, agreeing to give the inventor $150,000 ($5.81 million in 2025) to develop and build a wireless station on Long Island, capable of sending wireless messages to London as well as ships at sea.

claims.claim: The contract was signed in March 1901 and covered a wireless station capable of reaching London.
claims.quote: Morgan signed a contract with Tesla in March 1901, agreeing to give the inventor $150,000 ($5.81 million in 2025) to develop and build a wireless station on Long Island, capable of sending wireless messages to London as well as ships at sea.

claims.claim: Morgan took a 51% interest in the company and 51% of present and future patents from the project.
claims.where: card 3 headline and note; caption paragraph 1
claims.quote: The deal also included Morgan having a 51% interest in the company as well as a 51% share in present and future wireless patents developed from the project.

claims.claim: Tesla changed his plans after reading a June 1901 article by Marconi.
claims.quote: Tesla's plans changed radically after he read a June 1901 Electrical Review article by Marconi titled "Syntonic Wireless Telegraph".

claims.claim: Tesla scaled up to a far more powerful transmitter, with image and telephone transmission and wireless power delivery.
claims.quote: decided to scale up his designs with a much more powerful transmitter, incorporating his ideas of advanced telephone and image transmission as well as his ideas of wireless power delivery

claims.claim: Tesla decided a small Morse-code pilot system would not capture investors' attention.
claims.quote: Tesla, believing a small pilot system capable of sending Morse code yacht race results to Morgan in Europe would not be able to capture the attention of potential investors

claims.claim: Tesla wrote to Morgan in July 1901 asking for much more money, and Morgan refused and demanded an account of money already spent.
claims.quote: In July 1901, Tesla informed Morgan of his planned changes to the project and the need for much more money to build it. ... Morgan refused to lend additional funds and demanded an account of money already spent.

claims.claim: The 1904 photograph was taken so Tesla could return to J. P. Morgan for additional funds.
claims.quote: This 1904 photo of Wardenclyffe was taken so that Tesla could go back to J. P. Morgan to try and get the additional funds he needed to finish the tower.

claims.claim: In a July 1903 letter Tesla wrote: "Will you help me or let my great work — almost complete — go to pots?"
claims.quote: In a July 3, 1903 letter Tesla wrote "Will you help me or let my great work — almost complete — go to pots?"

claims.claim: Morgan declined again in reply to that letter.
claims.quote: Morgan's reply on July 14 was "I have received your letter and in reply would say that I should not feel disposed at present to make any further advances".

claims.claim: On the night of Morgan's reply and several nights after, newspapers reported the tower shooting bright flashes lighting up the sky.
claims.quote: The night of Morgan's reply, and several nights after, newspapers reported that the Wardenclyffe tower came alive shooting off bright flashes lighting up the night sky.

claims.claim: Tesla and his workers never explained the flashes, and the tower never seemed to operate again.
claims.quote: No explanation was forthcoming from Tesla or any of his workers as to the meaning of the display and Wardenclyffe never seemed to operate again.

claims.claim: The tower was dynamited for scrap beginning July 4, 1917, and was not fully demolished until September.
claims.quote: On July 4, 1917, the Smiley Steel Company of New York began demolition of the tower by dynamiting it. The tower was knocked on a tilt by the initial explosion but it was not totally demolished until September.

claims.claim: The scrap value realised was $1,750.
claims.quote: The scrap value realized was $1,750 (equivalent to $44,000 in 2025).

claims.claim: Tesla was unable to pay his mortgages and lost the property in foreclosure.
claims.quote: When Tesla was unable to make any further payments on the mortgages, Boldt foreclosed on the Wardenclyffe property.

claims.claim: Wartime rumours claimed the US Government ordered the tower demolished.
claims.quote: Since this was during World War I a rumor spread, picked up by newspapers and other publications, that the tower was demolished on orders of the United States Government with claims German spies were using it as a radio transmitter or observation post, or that it was being used as a landmark for German submarines.

claims.claim: The real reason for the demolition was debt Tesla had kept off the public record.
claims.quote: since the original mortgages with Boldt as well as the foreclosure had been kept off the public record in order to hide his financial difficulties, Tesla was not able to reveal the real reason for the demolition

claims.claim: Construction work beneath the tower was kept from the public and the press.
claims.quote: There was a great deal of construction under the tower to establish some form of ground connection, but Tesla and his workers kept the public and the press away from the project, so little is known.

claims.claim: There were four 100-foot tunnels radiating from a 120-foot shaft, and their purpose is still speculated on — drainage, access, or ground connection/resonance.
claims.quote: There is also contemporaneous and later descriptions of four 100 foot long tunnels, possibly brick lined and waterproofed, radiating from the bottom of the shaft north, south, east, and west terminating back at ground level in little brick igloos. Speculation on the tunnels ranges from them being for drainage, acting as access ways, or having the function of enhancing ground connection or resonance by interacting with the water table below the tower

claims.claim: How Tesla intended to combine the ground conduction method and the atmospheric method at Wardenclyffe is unknown.
claims.quote: How Tesla intended to employ the ground conduction method and atmospheric method in Wardenclyffe's design is unknown.

claims.claim: Tesla never scientifically tested his Earth-resonance theory.
claims.quote: Although Tesla demonstrated wireless power transmission at Colorado Springs, lighting electric lights mounted outside the building where he had his large experimental coil, he did not scientifically test his theories.
